question.:question/problem:
The region $R$ is enclosed inside the cylinder ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}=17$ between the surfaces $z=\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}$ and $z=9.$ Express the following triple integral in cylindrical polar coordinates. 

$$
{∭}_{R}\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}V
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
We will use the change of variables formula in the form

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,dV={∭}_{Δ}\,f(r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,z)\,r\,dz\,dr\,d\theta .
$$

If $(r,\theta ,z)$ are the cylindrical polar coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates $(x,y,z)$ can be found by using the formulas

$$
x=r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,y=r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,z=z.
$$

First, let's sketch the projection of $R$ onto the $xy$-plane:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/generate/scratch/17592186129267/images/projection-546bb4c73e967969511cb4587fe04736005c8e0df4e2f4750373f60cce65830d.png)

The region $R$ is a right vertical cylinder of radius $\sqrt{17}$ whose axis passes through the point $(0,0)$ in the $xy$-plane, and is

- bounded below by $z=\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}=r,$ and

- bounded above by $z=9.$

As a result, in cylindrical polar coordinates, our region can be expressed as 

$$
Δ=\{(r,\theta ,z)\,:\,0\le r\le \sqrt{17},\,0\le \theta <2\pi ,\,r\le z\le 9\}.
$$

Therefore, using the change of variables formula, we obtain  

$$
\begin{aligned}{∭}_{R}\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}V & ={∭}_{Δ}\sqrt{(r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta )^{2}+(r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )^{2}}\cdot r\,dz\,dr\,d\theta  \\  & ={∭}_{Δ}r\sqrt{{r}^{2}({cos}^{2}⁡\theta +{sin}^{2}⁡\theta )}\,dz\,dr\,d\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{17}}{\int }_{r}^{9}{r}^{2}\,dz\,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta .\end{aligned}
$$

\begin{aligned}\iiint_R z \left(x^{2} - y^{2}\right)\,\mathrm{d}V&=\iiint_\Delta z((r\cos\theta)^2-(r\sin\theta)^2)\cdot r\,dz\,dr\,d\theta \\ &=\iiint_\Delta rz(r^2\cos^2\theta-r^2\sin^2\theta)\,dz\,dr\,d\theta \\ &=\iiint_\Delta r^3z(\cos^2\theta-\sin^2\theta)\,dz\,dr\,d\theta \\ &=\iiint_\Delta r^3z\cos(2\theta)\,dz\,dr\,d\theta \\ &={\int }_{\frac{\pi}{2}}^{\pi}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{31}}{\int }_{r \cos{\left(\theta \right)}}^{r^{2} \sin^{2}{\left(\theta \right)} + 8}r^{3} z \cos{\left(2 \theta \right)}\,dz\,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta \end{aligned}
$$

knowledge_point.title: Rewriting a Triple Integral Defined Over a Cylindrical Solid

question.:question/problem:
The region $R$ is enclosed inside the cylinder $x^2+y^2=20$ for $x\le 0$ and $y\ge 0$, between the surfaces $z=x$ and $z=y^{2} + 6$. Express the following triple integral in cylindrical polar coordinates.

$$
\iiint_R z \left(x^{2} - y^{2}\right)\,\mathrm{d}V
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
We will use the change of variables formula in the form

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,dV={∭}_{Δ}\,f(r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,z)\,r\,dz\,dr\,d\theta .
$$

If $(r,\theta ,z)$ are the cylindrical polar coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates $(x,y,z)$ can be found by using the formulas

$$
x=r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,y=r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,z=z.
$$

First, let's sketch the projection of $R$ onto the $xy$-plane:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/generate/scratch/17592186129267/images/projection-7ab846c61be4d818041c7e46f899a03da1d0ae5a92b8058ac0f052089a6dbb6a.png)

The region $R$ is one-quarter of a right vertical cylinder of radius $2 \sqrt{5}$ whose axis passes through the point $(0,0)$ in the $xy$-plane, and is

- bounded below by $z=x=r \cos{\left(\theta \right)},$ and

- bounded above by $z=y^{2} + 6=r^{2} \sin^{2}{\left(\theta \right)} + 6.$

As a result, in cylindrical polar coordinates, our region can be expressed as

$$
\Delta=\{(r,\theta,z):0\le r\le 2 \sqrt{5},\frac{\pi}{2}\le\theta\le \pi,r \cos{\left(\theta \right)}\le z\le r^{2} \sin^{2}{\left(\theta \right)} + 6\}.
$$

Therefore, using the change of variables formula, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\iiint_R z \left(x^{2} - y^{2}\right)\,\mathrm{d}V&=\iiint_\Delta z((r\cos\theta)^2-(r\sin\theta)^2)\cdot r\,dz\,dr\,d\theta \\ &=\iiint_\Delta rz(r^2\cos^2\theta-r^2\sin^2\theta)\,dz\,dr\,d\theta \\ &=\iiint_\Delta r^3z(\cos^2\theta-\sin^2\theta)\,dz\,dr\,d\theta \\ &=\iiint_\Delta r^3z\cos(2\theta)\,dz\,dr\,d\theta \\ &={\int }_{\frac{\pi}{2}}^{\pi}{\int }_{0}^{2 \sqrt{5}}{\int }_{r \cos{\left(\theta \right)}}^{r^{2} \sin^{2}{\left(\theta \right)} + 6}r^{3} z \cos{\left(2 \theta \right)}\,dz\,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta \end{aligned}
$$
